resources.name: Central Texas Food Bank
resources.description: Get free groceries from many local food pantries. They also help you apply for SNAP (food stamps) and other food help. Most help is for people with low income in Central Texas. You can search for a pantry near 78702 on their website or call for help. Bring a photo ID and proof of where you live if you have it. No one is turned away in an emergency.
resources.availability_status: Open - pantry partners may have different hours, call or check website first

resources.name: El Buen Samaritano
resources.description: Get free groceries from a drive-thru food pantry. They also help with SNAP (food stamps) forms and other basic needs. Help is for people with low income in Travis County and nearby. You may need to show ID and say how many people live with you. Call or check online for pantry days and times before you go.
resources.availability_status: Open - pantry days and times change, call before visiting

resources.name: St. Vincent de Paul Society – Diocesan Council of Austin
resources.description: Get help with food, like grocery gift cards or pantry food, through local Catholic churches. Help is for people with low income in many Central Texas zip codes. You do not have to be Catholic. Call their main number or use the website to find the church group for your zip code. They may also help with rent or bills if funds are open.
resources.availability_status: Open - help depends on funds in each church group, call first

resources.name: Sunrise Homeless Navigation Center (Sunrise Church Austin)
resources.description: Get free hot breakfast and other basic needs if you are homeless or very low income. They offer meals, showers, mail, and help finding other places. People who are housed but struggling can also ask for food help. No ID is needed for meals. Check hours before you go, as meal times can change.
resources.availability_status: Open - meal and drop-in hours limited, check website or call

resources.name: SAFE Alliance – Food and Basic Needs for Clients
resources.description: Get food, diapers, and basic needs if you are a survivor of family or sexual violence. Help is for adults, teens, and children who are getting help from SAFE. You can call their 24-hour line to ask how to start. They may offer shelter, legal help, and support, plus food while you are in their programs.
resources.availability_status: Open - some programs may have waitlists, call hotline first

resources.name: Austin Public Health – WIC (Women, Infants, and Children) Program
resources.description: Get free healthy food, baby formula, and nutrition help if you are pregnant, just had a baby, or have a child under age 5. WIC is for people with low income who meet program rules. They give food benefits on a card you use at the store. They also give breastfeeding help and simple health checks. Call to see if you qualify and to set a first visit.
resources.address: WIC East 2nd Street Clinic, 1000 E 2nd St, Austin, TX 78702
resources.availability_status: Open - must qualify for WIC, call for a first visit

resources.description: Get help with rent, light, gas, or water bills if you live in Central Texas. Help is given through local Catholic churches. You do not have to be Catholic. They may also help you find other places for more help. Ask how to send your papers by photo or email if you cannot visit.
resources.availability_status: Help depends on funds - call to check current help

resources.description: Get short-term help with rent or utility bills if you live in their area. This parish helps people in parts of Central Austin. Help depends on money they have. Call and leave a message with your name, address, phone, and what you need. A volunteer will call you back to ask more questions. They may ask for your lease, ID, and your bill. They can also suggest other places that may help with housing and bills.
resources.availability_status: Funds change month to month - call to see if help is open

resources.name: Travis County Health and Human Services – Family Support Services
resources.description: Get help paying rent, mortgage, or utility bills if you live in Travis County. This county office helps low income people who meet income rules. They may help with electric, gas, water, or rent to stop loss of housing. You must apply and share income, ID, and bills. You may need an online form or visit. Call first to ask how to apply and what papers you need. Ask about help for your ZIP code 78741.
resources.availability_status: Often high demand - help may be limited or waitlisted

resources.name: City of Austin – Customer Assistance Programs for Utilities
resources.description: Get help lowering your City of Austin electric, water, and trash bills if you qualify. You must live in the Austin city limits and get bills from Austin Energy or Austin Water. Help can be a monthly discount or one-time bill help. Some programs are for people with low income, seniors, or people with disabilities. You may be signed up through other help like SNAP (food stamps). Call to see if you already get a discount or can apply.
resources.availability_status: Ongoing program - discounts may take one to two bills to start

resources.name: Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs – Help for Rent and Utilities (Statewide)
resources.description: Find state programs that help with rent, light, gas, or water bills in Texas. This state office does not give money directly. It shows local groups that do. You can search by ZIP code 78741 on their site. You can also learn about weatherization help to lower bills. Call if you need help using the website or finding local groups. They can point you to open programs near you.
resources.availability_status: Programs change often - call or check site for current options

resources.name: Catholic Charities of Central Texas – Financial Stability Program
resources.description: Get short-term help with rent or utility bills and money coaching. This group helps low income people in Central Texas, no matter your faith. Help depends on money they have and your income. You may meet by phone or online. They will ask about your bills, income, and goals. They may pay part of a bill or rent one time. They can also help you plan a budget and find other places for housing help.
resources.availability_status: Often has waitlist - call or check online form for current status
